title: Seat a gift-box lid squarely
instruction: Put the lid fully onto the gift box, level and square. Keep the gift inside and leave the box where it is. Let go when it is seated.
context: Closing a two-piece gift box is a familiar precision placement. The lid's skirt slips over the outside of the base with only about 2 mm clearance on each side, so the lid must come down level and square: lowered at a slant, a skirt edge catches the rim and wedges; pushed down, the light packed box slides away. There is no click or latch to confirm it; the lid seats by gravity when it is aligned, and the hand must let go without dragging it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station, fixed layout and object_jitter=0. Coordinates are metres: x forward from the midpoint between arm bases, y to the robot's left, z above the table. The burgundy base is the supplied original base.stl/base.usda design: solid PLA, outside 100 x 66 x 40 mm, cavity 96 x 62 x 38 mm, floor and walls 2 mm, model-derived mass 46.90176 g, centred at (0.24, -0.10), open side up. The matching burgundy lid is the supplied lid.stl/lid.usda design: solid PLA, outside 112 x 78 x 28 mm, inside 104 x 70 x 26 mm, top 2 mm and four skirt walls 4 mm, model-derived mass 68.60672 g, centred at (0.20, -0.26), top up and skirt down. Both long axes follow x and both are movable compound rigid bodies with one convex collider per panel. Centred design clearance is 2 mm on each of the four sides. A plain oak gift block, 60 x 38 x 20 mm and 31.92 g at assumed density 700 kg/m^3, lies flat inside the base with the same horizontal centre. Base and lid spawn 1 mm above the table; the gift spawns 1 mm above the initial base floor. Print both box parts in PLA at 100 percent infill, 0.2 mm layers and 0.4 mm nozzle, allowing +/-0.2 mm linear dimension error; print the lid top-down, then invert for setup. Dimensions come from design files and have not been physically measured. No commercial cardboard-box equivalence is claimed.
scoring:
Real trials: award the highest satisfied final-state tier, never sum tiers; all other outcomes score 0. Use a millimetre ruler, a straightedge and level side/top photos; use the trial video to confirm release, no dragging, a stationary base and a gift that stays inside. Mark the initial base outline; movement over 20 mm is a failure, not permission to deliberately reposition it. Let Hr be the current base-rim height above the table, Ht the mean height of the four lid-top corners, C the horizontal centre distance measured to +/-1 mm, and Dh the highest minus lowest lid-top corner height. A seated lid has Ht = Hr + 2 mm +/-1.5 mm. Full credit: seated height, C <=2 mm, Dh <=2 mm (about 1 degree over the 112 mm lid length), gap-skew difference G <=2.9 mm (about 1.5 degrees yaw), all four side gaps visible and nonzero, hands released and clear, and stable for 1 s. 0.75: the same seated height and C <=2 mm, Dh <=4 mm (about 2 degrees), G <=5.8 mm (about 3 degrees), all four gaps visible and nonzero, but no full-credit award. 0.5: an upright, partly engaged lid with Hr +0.5 mm <= Ht <= Hr +18 mm and C <=8 mm, with no higher award. 0.25: an upright lid resting at the rim with Ht = Hr +28 mm +/-2 mm and C <=25 mm, with no higher award. The base must remain upright and resting on the table, and the shared exclusions below apply. Height conversions use the 28 mm outer lid height, 26 mm skirt and 2 mm top: Ht-Hr = 28 mm - engagement, so engagement from 10 to 26+1.5 mm gives 0.5 to 18 mm; zero engagement gives 28 +/-2 mm. Along the 112 mm long edge, 112 sin(1 degree)=1.955 mm and 112 sin(2 degrees)=3.909 mm motivate the 2/4 mm corner-height checks. For the actual 112 x78 mm top, Dh=112|R31|+78|R32| mm, where R is the lid orientation relative to the table; at tilt angle theta its worst direction gives sqrt(112^2+78^2) sin(theta), or 2.382/4.763 mm at 1/2 degrees. Thus the ruler checks are approximate observable criteria, not exact equivalents of every 3-D tilt. For yaw, measure opposite long-side gaps g+ and g- at both ends of a 100 mm baseline along the base, extending the straight edge lines with a ruler if needed. Define Dnear=(g+-g-)near, Dfar=(g+-g-)far and G=112/(2x100)|Dfar-Dnear| mm. This cancels translation and normalizes the gap-skew difference to the 112 mm lid length: G=112 tan(|yaw|), giving 2.933 mm at 1.5 degrees and 5.870 mm at 3 degrees; use the conservative 2.9/5.8 mm limits. A single opposed-gap difference without this two-end construction measures offset as well as yaw. A ruler or photo cannot reliably resolve sub-millimetre centring; the 2 mm per-side cavity clearance already constrains a seated lid to about 2 mm offset on each axis. The radial C <=2 mm check is conservative for diagonal offsets and confirms that the lid surrounds the base.

Simulation implementation (unchanged thresholds): all automatic credit requires valid initial/state data, no latched violation, still objects, both complete grippers at least 30 mm from all objects, and readable gripper states. The base must finish within 3 mm of its table-resting height and within 2 degrees of upright. The scorer uses top=lid centre z+14 mm and bottom=lid centre z-14 mm; compared with the actual mean top-corner height, top differs by 14(1-cos(tilt)) mm (0.0021 mm at 1 degree and 0.0085 mm at 2 degrees). 0.25 requires |bottom-rim| <=2 mm, centre <=25 mm and tilt <=5 degrees. 0.5 requires engagement >=10 mm and no deeper than 26+1.5 mm, centre <=8 mm and tilt <=10 degrees. 0.75 requires |top-(rim+2 mm)| <=1.5 mm, centre <=2 mm, relative yaw <=3 degrees and tilt <=2 degrees. Full success additionally requires centre <=2 mm, relative yaw <=1.5 degrees and tilt <=1 degree continuously for 1 s. The 0.75 and full tiers share the 2 mm centre bound; angular alignment and the completed hold distinguish them. These orientation checks remain unchanged and are not replaced by the ruler proxies. Highest-tier precedence makes awards exclusive. More than 20 mm of base displacement, base/lid toppling beyond 15/30 degrees, a box more than 10 mm below the table, any object speed above 0.75 m/s, the gift leaving the base interior (1 mm numerical margin), an unexplained >100 mm one-step jump, or invalid initial/state data is latched to zero. Stillness uses the last ten positions (every sample within 2 mm) and orientations (0.5 degrees); before filling the window it uses speed <=10 mm/s and spin <=0.10 rad/s. Only a >100 mm single-step jump that returns the complete nominal layout resets the episode; slowly restoring objects does not clear latches. score() and distance() are read-only; score() never returns more than 0.75, and the framework awards 1.0 after the success hold. In video review mode, object-only partial credit is capped at 0.75 and automatic full success is disabled until release is checked manually.
run_limit: 1200 control steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz); demonstrated demo completion in 533 steps, giving a 2.251x margin.
fidelity: Original printable PLA geometry, not a cardboard material model. Both parts have actual cavities, five primitive convex colliders, and a mass/centre of mass integrated from a watertight STL at assumed solid PLA density 1240 kg/m^3. No flex, dents, adhesion, paper wrapping, trapped-air suction or manufacturing warp is modelled. Dimensions and per-side clearance come from design files; no physical specimen has been measured. At commit 253f934, the right-arm scripted demo scored 1.0 in 533 steps and Dream-1 scored 0.0 after 1200 steps, both at seed 0 with object_jitter=0. Earlier demo3 diagnostics at commit 9a03999 measured a seated top-height error of -0.006421 mm, tilt 0.002152 degrees, relative yaw 0.065305 degrees and centre offset 0.889511 mm at step 520; final framework success was at step 533. The minimum side clearance at second-descent entry was only 0.450874 mm, below the 1 mm diagnostic target. That diagnostic is not a score gate. Successful nominal execution does not calibrate threshold boundaries or establish robustness beyond seed 0. Automatic pose and hand clearance establish a geometric end condition, not a force/contact measurement. Inherited contact offset 5 mm, rest offset zero and static/dynamic friction 1.2/1.0 remain physically uncalibrated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1200/1200 steps, max_steps); demo: 1.0 (533 steps, success)
reset_notes: Return the open base and top-up lid to the stated centres and yaw; lay the wooden gift flat inside the base. Inspect actual printed dimensions and all four side clearances before real trials; no sample has been measured yet. Replace a warped or damaged pair. A new episode clears latched violations only on a single-step position change greater than 100 mm while the complete layout returns to nominal; slowly rearranging objects does not clear history.
